podcast.title: Band Breakup
podcast.body: Sandbox broke up when one of its members decided to pursue medical school instead of continuing with the group. "Sandbox won three East Coast Music Awards and were nominated for a Juno before they broke up and one of the guys in the band decided he'd rather go to medical school than be in a group."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Breakup Due to Label Interference
podcast.body: The band broke up because their record company disapproved of the new direction taken on their second album in 1997. Rather than compromise their artistic vision, they chose to disband. "They didn't like the sound of the band's new direction. And so, rather than been to that, well, they broke up."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Jason Archibald's Post-Band Career
podcast.body: Jason Archibald, a former member of Sandbox, pursued a career in medicine, graduating from Dalhousie University as a doctor in 2001. This marks a significant transition from music to a professional career. "Jason Archibald is now a doctor. He graduated from Dell House of University in 2001."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Mike Smith's Post-Band Career (Trailer Park Boys)
podcast.body: Guitarist Mike Smith transitioned from music to acting and comedy, co-founding The Trailer Park Boys and becoming widely known for his portrayal of the character Bubbles in the Sunnyvale trailer park series. This represents a significant career shift. "then there's guitarist Mike Smith. He's doing fine. He made up with a couple of other guys and founded the trailer park boys."

podcast.title: Mike Smith's Transition to Bubbles
podcast.body: Mike Smith, a guitarist for Sandbox, took a job as a sound man in movies and television after the band's breakup. He developed a character using a pair of very thick glasses that a girlfriend found for him in a Texas flea market. While goofing around on the set of the 1999 movie "The Trailer Park Boys," everyone liked the character so much that they wrote Mike into the movie, leading him to become "Bubbles, the trailer park boy." "Mike Smith, one of the guitarists, took a job as a sound man in movies and television. He had this character that he did using a pair of really thick glasses, a girlfriend found for him in a Texas flea market. And we'll goofing around on the set of a 1999 movie called The Trailer Park Boys. Everyone really liked the character so much that they wrote Mike into the movie. And this is how Mike Smith guitarist from the Juno nominated Sandbox became Bubbles, the trailer park boy who now sings songs like..."

podcast.title: Origin and Record Deal
podcast.body: Sandbox originated from New Glasgow, Nova Scotia, and secured a record deal with Vancouver's Network Records after submitting demos. This agreement facilitated the release of their debut album. "Sandbox was from New Glasgow, Nova Scotia, and after sending out some demos, they nailed down a deal with Vancouver's network records."

podcast.title: Paul Murray's Family Connection
podcast.body: Singer Paul Murray is noted as the nephew of the renowned singer Ann Murray, establishing a familial link to another prominent figure in Canadian music. His current whereabouts were not explicitly known. "singer Paul Murray is, although I can tell you he's the nephew of singer Ann Murray."

podcast.title: Scott McFarland's Continued Music Work
podcast.body: Bass player Scott McFarland has continued to work in music since Sandbox's breakup, regularly picking up side band gigs. This indicates his ongoing involvement in the music industry. "bass player Scott McFarland continues to work in music, picking up side band gigs."
